newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TWO RED WINGS PLAYERS INJURED IN SERIOUS LIMO CRASH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TWO RED WINGS PLAYERS INJURED IN SERIOUS LIMO CRASH.

text.p: Two key Russian members of the Detroit Red Wings were among four people injured in a serious limousine accident Friday night, less than a week after the team won the NHL's Stanley Cup championship.

Defenceman Vladimir Konstantinov was in intensive care with severe head injuries and was put on a ventilator, while defenceman Viacheslav Fetisov was listed in fair condition with chest injuries, according to emergency room doctors at William Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak, Michigan.
"Mr. Konstantinov has had a significant head injury. We will require days to assess the seriousness of his head injuries," said Dr. James Cisek, who described the injuries as life-threatening.
Both players were former Soviet stars and members of the Red Wings' vaunted "Russian Five" unit that played so brilliantly in Detroit's run to its first Stanley Cup since 1955.
Also injured was the team's masseur, Sergei Mnatsakanov, who was listed in serious condition with life-threatening head injuries, Cisek said.
The limousine's driver, Richard Gnida, received minor injuries and was being kept overnight for observation.

The accident occurred at about 9:15 p.m. EDT (0215 gmt) as the players were returning from a golf outing that was supposed to be the Red Wings' last gathering before the players broke up for the summer.
According to broadcast reports, the limousine struck a tree after swerving to avoid a stalled truck that did not have its hazard lights on.
Team owner Michael Ilitch and several Red Wings players arrived at the hospital shortly after word of the accident was broadcast over local media.
The accident comes at the end of an intense week of Detroit-area celebrations for the Red Wings, who last Saturday completed a four-game sweep of the Philadelphia Flyers to win the Stanley Cup.
Fetisov, 39, considered one of the former Soviet Union's all-time greatest hockey players, was one of the first Russians to play in the NHL, joining the North Amerian league in 1989.
The tough as nails Konstantinov, 30, anchored Detroit's sensational defensive effort throughout the playoffs.
